found_values.value: One output of the I/O expander per biased line, 5 in all: the 4 multiprotocol ports and the UART socket. A resistor holds each control input at the pull-down selection, so the reset and unpowered state selects the pull-down (V57's condition). The expander resets with the RP2354B and its driving pin is then an input (IOBoard.md:340). A jumper cannot follow a mode firmware sets per binding (IOBoard.md:64, :230). A circuit with no control input cannot tell the modes apart: bidirectional DShot and the UART-based modes idle high, servo PWM, PPM and plain DShot idle low (IOBoard.md:251, :253, :256). An RP2354B GPIO also meets V57, because Bank 0 pads reset pulled low (section 9.3), and costs 5 GPIO. The expander's output count is V119 (R6)

found_values.value: Low, on every gated line, while the RP2354B is held in reset and while it restarts through the watchdog. In a RUN-pin or brownout reset the pads return to their reset state (section 9.3): output high impedance, input disabled, pulled low at 36 to 113 kOhm (Table 1436), IO muxing at the null function. A 244's inputs then read low (+-5 uA through 113 kOhm is 0.57 V, under V_IL 0.8 V) and it drives low; the switch passes the pad's low; the 10 kOhm pull-down holds the line; the expander resets with the RP2354B and the control resistors select the pull-down. Section 9.3's list of events that return the pads to reset (brownout, RUN low, two SWD resets) does not name the watchdog; through a watchdog reset the pads return to the same state only when the watchdog's reset reaches RESETS: pico-sdk's _watchdog_enable sets PSM_WDSEL for every stage except ROSC and XOSC (section 12.9.6.1); PSM WDSEL bit 4 is RESETS (Table 532); RESETS resets with PADS_BANK0 and IO_BANK0 held (Table 535); resetting the PADS register block returns non-isolated pads to their reset state (section 9.7). Firmware that leaves RESETS out of PSM_WDSEL leaves the pads, and the connector, at their pre-reset level. Not established: the effect of POWMAN_WDSEL.RESET_SWCORE (Table 490, reset 0x0)

found_values.value: Both faults, continuous: a short to ground, and a short to the port's supply pin at up to 8.7 V (F16). The lead carries signal, ground and rail in one plug (IOBoard.md:531) and nothing in the tree limits the current into a shorted signal line (IOBoard.md:536). Series resistance per gated line between the gate element and the connector, with the clamp and the bias network on the gate element's side. Lower bounds: a line driven by the RP2354B pad through the switch takes at least 275 Ohm (3.3 V / 12 mA, the highest drive setting Table 1436 characterises; 283 Ohm at the 3.399 V rail ceiling); a line driven by a 244 takes at least 142 Ohm (3.4 V / 24 mA). Upper bound on the multiprotocol and UART lines in servo configuration mode: the servo's open-drain low reaches the pin at V = (3.3/1000 + Vs/R) / (1/1000 + 1/10000 + 1/R) = 0.70 V + 0.77 Vs at 275 Ohm, at or under V_IL 0.8 V only while the servo's output-low voltage Vs is 0.13 V or less; no source read states that voltage. A short to 8.7 V puts (8.7 - 3.6) / 275 = 18.5 mA into a 3.6 V clamp and 95 mW into the resistor. The resistor and the clamp are round 2 parts

found_values.value: A STOP, then the operator clear of the F11 latch; no separate switch. The ESC pack switch and the buffer enable both follow the enable node alone (Research.md:281); the pack switch closes within 500 ms of the enable rising (V46), and the gate enables at once. With the programming mode bound before the clear, the RP2354B holds the line high with the pull-up selected, so the ESC powers up with its line high. AM32 stays in its bootloader only when the line never reads low while it samples with its pull-down and then its pull-up (checkForSignal). BLHeli_S's bootloader waits while the line is high (wait_for_low) and exits about 250 ms (BOOT_DELAY) after it goes low without a signature. ESCape32 needs the line high for 2 s at start-up. A Hitec D-series servo needs no power cycle: firmware writes its REBOOT register and it accepts serial 1000 ms later. VESC: no source read asks for a power cycle

report.value: A programming session switches no supply of its own. The ESC powers up with its line high after a STOP and the operator clear of the F11 latch: the pack switch and the buffer enable follow the enable node (pack switch closed within 500 ms, V46), and the RP2354B holds the line high through the selected 1 kOhm pull-up. AM32 needs the line never low at start-up, BLHeli_S waits while it is high, ESCape32 needs it high for 2 s. A Hitec D-series servo needs no power cycle: a REBOOT register write, then 1000 ms. VESC: no source read asks for a power cycle
report.source: V78 (found, sources read 2026-09-29T04:41:00Z to 04:41:02Z); Research.md:281, :606 at e13f5f60

report.figure: connector level in RP2354B reset (RUN, brownout)
report.value: Low on all 21 gated lines (16 PWM, 4 multiprotocol, UART socket). Pads at high impedance, pulled low at 36 to 113 kOhm (section 9.3, Table 1436). SN74LVC244A II +-5 uA gives 0.57 V through 113 kOhm, under V_IL 0.8 V, so the 244 drives low; SN74CBTLV3126 passes the pad's low with the 10 kOhm pull-down; the expander resets with the RP2354B and each SN74LVC1G126 OE pull-down gives Z, so the pull-down alone biases the line. The receiver input's SN74LVC1T45 DIR is held low: receive
report.source: RP2350 datasheet build-date 2025-07-29, https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/rp2350/rp2350-datasheet.pdf, section 9.3 and Table 1436, re-read 2026-09-29T04:39:31Z; SCAS414AG 5.5 re-read 04:40:31Z; SCDS038N Table 7-1; SCES224S Table 7-1; SCES515N Table 7-1; IOBoard.md:340

report.figure: connector level through a watchdog reset
report.value: Low, as in a RUN reset, only when the watchdog's reset reaches RESETS. Section 9.3 lists brownout, RUN low and two SWD resets as the events that return pads to reset, not the watchdog. pico-sdk's _watchdog_enable sets PSM_WDSEL for every stage except ROSC and XOSC (12.9.6.1); WDSEL bit 4 is RESETS (Table 532); RESETS resets holding PADS_BANK0 and IO_BANK0 (Table 535); a PADS reset returns non-isolated pads to their reset state (9.7). Firmware that leaves RESETS out of PSM_WDSEL leaves the pads, and the connector, at their pre-reset level: a firmware requirement for P5. Not established: POWMAN_WDSEL.RESET_SWCORE (Table 490). The tree enables no watchdog yet (IOBoard.md:221)
report.source: RP2350 sections 9.3, 9.7 re-read 2026-09-29T04:39:31Z; 12.9.6.1 and Tables 490, 532, 535 as FU-A2 read them at 00:10:21Z (confirmed by the FU-A2 datasheet verifier)

report.figure: connector high level against device input thresholds
report.value: Thresholds: STM32F051 2.31 V (0.7 x 3.3 V), EFM8BB21 2.7 V (VDD 3.3 V - 0.6 V), Hitec D-series about 2 V; an ATmega8 ESC at 5.0 V 3.0 V (not a family the tree names). Guaranteed highs: SN74LVC244A VCC - 0.2 V = 3.0 V at -100 uA (VCC 3.201 V), 2.4 V at -12 mA (VCC 3 V); the RP2354B pad 2.62 V min at its rated 2 to 12 mA, passed rail to rail by SN74CBTLV3126. The connector load is about 0.32 mA (10 kOhm pull-down); no datasheet row sits at that current, and RP2350 Figure 150 is typical only. So: STM32F051 is met on both paths by every row; EFM8BB21's 2.7 V is met by the 244's 100 uA row but not shown at 0.32 mA, and not shown on the switch path in pull-down modes (plain DShot, servo PWM on a multiprotocol port), where 2.62 V is the only guaranteed figure; in pull-up modes the 1 kOhm pull-up holds 3.0 V. An ATmega8 ESC at 5.0 V has 0 V margin at the 244's 100 uA row. EFM8BB21 pins are 5 V tolerant (5.8 V maximum at VDD above 3.3 V), so a 5 V drive is an option the owner may weigh; V63 as found needs none
